relations.rel:includes: import another entry's lights only, never its predicate
relations.rel:conditional_includes: import lights when the stated `when` holds; `one_of` is a set of legal alternatives among which the vessel picks one
relations.rel:in_lieu_of: this entry's lights replace the referenced entries' lights
relations.rel:excludes: the referenced entries must not be shown at the same time
relations.rel:exempts: the referenced entries are not required
relations.rel:overrides: the superiority relation: the referencing norm's obligation displaces the referenced norm's when both apply

modalities.shall-if-practicable: mandatory where practicable, with a stated fallback
modalities.conditional: modality depends on facts; see modality_by
modalities.exempt: the entry relieves a requirement rather than imposing one
modalities.shall-not-impede: a distinct duty to avoid impeding another vessel, not a negated shall

categories.standard: produces technical values (ranges, heights); not evaluated
categories.scope: reads visibility, in-sight, jurisdiction; the engine derives which sections apply
categories.display: reads one vessel's facts; the engine derives signals and modality
categories.classification: reads relative geometry and history; the engine derives encounter type and risk of collision
categories.precedence: reads two vessels' facts plus encounter type; the engine derives give-way/stand-on/shall-not-impede/none
categories.conduct: reads encounter, role, phase, kinematics and observations; monitored over a trace, not evaluated at a point
categories.care: reads anything; produces residual responsibility; represented, never independently evaluated
categories.meta: reads the region state; produces a banner and advisories; computed by a solver, reviewed by humans

effects.note: What a two-subject entry produces, as a role per subject: `effect` is {"own": <role>, "other": <role>} for a `precedence` entry, and {"part", "section", "applies_rules"} for a `scope` entry. A `display` entry has no `effect`; its output is `lights`. The roles are a closed vocabulary and are not identifiers (docs/identifiers.md, 'What is not an identifier'). Pencil: ADR 0005 and docs/identifiers.md.

roles.give-way: this subject shall keep out of the way of the other; Rule 16 governs the action
roles.stand-on: this subject shall keep her course and speed; Rule 17 governs, including 17(a)(ii) and 17(b)
roles.shall-not-impede: this subject shall not impede the other's passage or safe passage; Rule 8(f) governs, and by 8(f)(iii) it confers nothing on the other
roles.keep-clear: this subject shall keep well clear of the other and avoid impeding her navigation, outside the give-way/stand-on pairing (18(e), 18(f)(i))
roles.none: this paragraph confers no role on this subject. Recorded rather than omitted: `none` on the counterpart of a shall-not-impede duty is the content of 8(f)(iii), and `none` on both sides of a NUC/RAM pair is the content of Rule 18's partial order.

known_omissions.what: A power-driven vessel to which 24(a) or (c) applies shall also comply with 23(a)(ii) — the second masthead light.
known_omissions.why: Not an entry in the settled table; 24a-m2/24a-m3 carry in_lieu_of against 23a1 and 23a2 instead. Recorded here rather than added unilaterally.

known_omissions.what: Vessels pushed or towed in a group; inconspicuous partly submerged tows; impracticability fallbacks.
known_omissions.why: Outside the settled table. Rule text is present in rules.json.

known_omissions.what: Towing operation that severely restricts the tow's ability to deviate: Rule 24(a) lights plus the 27(b)(i)/(ii) RAM display.
known_omissions.why: Outside the settled table; expressible as activity=towing plus activity=ram.

known_omissions.what: Vessels under 12 m, except when diving, need not exhibit the Rule 27 lights and shapes.
known_omissions.why: A cross-cutting exemption over the whole 27 family; no entry in the table.

known_omissions.what: Seaplanes and WIG craft show the closest practicable equivalent.
known_omissions.why: Not expressible as a light set.

known_omissions.what: A vessel shall not cross a narrow channel or fairway if such crossing impedes the passage of a vessel which can safely navigate only within that channel.
known_omissions.why: The duty is conditioned on own crossing the channel, which is a relation between own's heading and the channel's axis. Neither the channel's axis nor 'crossing it' is a fact this package carries, and `pair:env:narrow_channel` is a boolean about the place, not a geometry. No entry rather than an entry whose predicate is not the paragraph's.

known_omissions.what: A vessel constrained by her draft shall navigate with particular caution having full regard to her special condition.
known_omissions.why: `conduct`, not `precedence`: it prescribes a manner of navigating rather than a role in a pair, and conduct is monitored over a trace rather than evaluated at a point (ADR 0005 sec. 1). No conduct entry shape exists yet.

known_omissions.what: A seaplane on the water shall in general keep well clear of all vessels and avoid impeding their navigation; where risk of collision exists she shall comply with Rules 4-19.
known_omissions.why: There is no fact for being a seaplane. `fact:propulsion` has power, sail and oars, and Rule 3(a) makes a seaplane a vessel without giving the fact record anywhere to say so. The effect vocabulary has `keep-clear` for it; the predicate does not exist.

known_omissions.what: A WIG craft operating on the water surface shall comply with Rules 4-19 as a power-driven vessel.
known_omissions.why: Not a precedence norm: it maps a WIG on the surface onto `propulsion:power` for the rest of Part B, which is a classification or a decode-table statement rather than a role in a pair. 18(f)(i) -- the phase that does change the roles -- is entry 18f1.

known_omissions.what: The remaining `scope` paragraphs: the waters the Rules apply to, special rules made by an authority, the adoption of traffic separation schemes, the special-construction determination, and the sunset-to-sunrise and restricted-visibility gates on the light rules.
known_omissions.why: None of them reads a fact this package declares. 1(a) needs a fact about the waters; 1(b)/(c)/(e) are about an authority's determination, which is closer to the jurisdiction dimension of ADR 0001 than to a predicate; 1(d) is not addressed to a vessel at all; 20(b)/(c) need time of day and visibility, and applicability.json's `conditions` note already records that night is assumed rather than gated. Deferred to a later PR with 4, 11 and 19(a) landing first.

represented_paragraphs.note: Residual responsibility for every other paragraph; nothing in this package discharges it, so it is recorded rather than dropped from the model.

entries.note: Part B Section I is ungated: the predicate is empty because 'any condition of visibility' is the absence of a condition, not a fact. A scope entry is never a display entry, so an empty `when` selects no lights.
Rule 3(k)'s in-sight test is a fact of the pair, so Section II is gated on `pair:geo:in_sight` and every Rule 18 entry below repeats that gate rather than relying on the engine to apply this one.

entries.gap: 19(a) is 'not in sight of one another AND navigating in or near an area of restricted visibility'. Only the first conjunct is a fact; there is no fact for being in or near an area of restricted visibility, and it is a property of the water rather than of either vessel or of the pair's geometry. This entry is therefore wider than the paragraph: it selects Section III for any pair not in sight. Recorded rather than silently narrowed.
entries.note: The complement of 11. Rule 3(l) defines restricted visibility; nothing in facts.json carries it.

Own's activity is listed positively because the predicate language has no negation: a power-driven vessel that is herself NUC, RAM or fishing is ranked by 18(c) or by nothing, not by 18(a). `activity:cbd` is in the list deliberately -- 18(d) protects a CBD vessel, it does not rank her.

`activity:mine` (27(f)) and `activity:diving` (27(e)) are listed alongside `activity:ram` because Rule 3(g) enumerates mine clearance and underwater operations as restricted-in-ability-to-manoeuvre. `activity:ram_underwater` is matched by `activity:ram` under the refinement rule and is listed only for readability.
`activity:trawling` is listed beside `activity:fishing`: the evaluator refines only ram -> ram_underwater, so a predicate written for `activity:fishing` does not otherwise reach a trawler.
A sailing vessel that is also fishing is ranked by 18(a)(iii), so own's counterpart here is restricted to the ordinary activities.
'so far as possible' is the practicability qualifier, so the modality is shall-if-practicable. 18(c) does not distinguish propulsion: a fishing vessel under sail is ranked here, not by 18(b).

`other` is `none` and not `stand-on`: 18(d) confers no stand-on role, which is the point 8(f)(iii) makes explicit. Own's list is 'any vessel other than a vessel not under command or a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre', written positively for want of negation.
entries.gap: 18(d)(i) reads 'shall, if the circumstances of the case admit, avoid impeding'. That is two deontic qualifications at once -- a practicability caveat and a shall-not-impede duty -- and `modality` is a single closed value. shall-not-impede is kept because it is the distinctive one; the 'if the circumstances of the case admit' half is lost. The paragraph also conditions on the CBD vessel 'exhibiting the signals in Rule 28', which is a display fact of the other vessel and is not read here.

entries.note: A WIG craft near the surface also satisfies 18(a)'s predicate (she is a power-driven vessel underway), so 18(f)(i) carries rel:overrides against the 18(a) family and 18(d)(i). `keep-clear` is one effect for the paragraph's two duties -- keep well clear, and avoid impeding navigation -- which the effect vocabulary cannot separate.

Recorded as a precedence norm rather than as a rel:overrides. It is not a superiority relation: 8(f)(ii) keeps the impeding vessel's duty alive, so nothing is displaced. What 8(f)(iii) does is deny the not-to-be-impeded vessel any role -- `none` on both sides -- so that shall-not-impede is never read as conferring stand-on.
entries.gap: The paragraph's antecedent is 'a vessel, the passage of which is not to be impeded'. That is the output of another norm, not a fact, and a precedence predicate reads only facts. The `when` is therefore the risk-of-collision half alone, which makes this entry wider than the paragraph: it applies to any pair with risk of collision. Kept wide and recorded rather than narrowed by inventing a fact.
entries.no_gate_note: No in-sight gate: Rule 4 puts Rules 4-10 in any condition of visibility.

entries.note: Categorised `precedence`, not `classification` as ADR 0005 sec. 1 and the proposal's first-cut table have it. 13(a) is the one paragraph of Rule 13 that assigns a role, and a `classification` entry has no field to put a role in; 13(b)'s sector test is the classification and is what sets the latch. Q-14 settles membership paragraph by paragraph and this is one of them.
entries.gap: The predicate reads `own:hist:was_overtaking` alone, so the instantaneous 13(b) sector test -- `other:geo:rel_bearing_deg` in (112.5, 247.5) -- is not modelled here. A `classification` entry for 13(b) is what would set the latch, and none exists yet; a consumer must set the fact itself. Written this way because a `when` has no disjunction, so 'in the sector OR latched' cannot be one entry, and the latched form is the one 13(d) makes load-bearing.

The vessel whose passage is not to be impeded is identified by the paragraph as one 'which can safely navigate only within a narrow channel or fairway'. That is a property of the other vessel against the water, and no fact carries it. This entry therefore asserts a duty toward `other` whenever the encounter is in a narrow channel, which may be a duty toward a third vessel instead. Recorded rather than narrowed.
entries.note: 9(b) has a disjunctive subject -- under 20 m OR a sailing vessel -- and a `when` is a conjunction, so the paragraph takes two entries. This is the length half.

entries.gap: The vessel whose passage is not to be impeded is identified by the paragraph as one 'which can safely navigate only within a narrow channel or fairway'. That is a property of the other vessel against the water, and no fact carries it. This entry therefore asserts a duty toward `other` whenever the encounter is in a narrow channel, which may be a duty toward a third vessel instead. Recorded rather than narrowed.
entries.note: The sailing half of 9(b). Its rel:overrides against 18(a)(iv) is the substantive one: outside a channel a power-driven vessel keeps out of the way of a sailing vessel, and inside one the sailing vessel must not impede her.

Reverses 18(a)(iii) and 18(b)(iii) inside a narrow channel: 9(c)'s object is 'any other vessel navigating within a narrow channel or fairway', so unlike 9(b) it needs no further fact about the other vessel.

entries.gap: 'any vessel following a traffic lane' is unmodelled for the other vessel; `pair:env:traffic_lane` says the encounter is in a lane, not that the other vessel is following it.
